title: Parameterize a libpq query
summary: Replace SQL built by string formatting with PQexecParams, always call PQclear, and check a SELECT against PGRES_TUPLES_OK.

turns.user: find_user_id breaks for users with a ' in their email. also memory seems to creep up when it runs for a long time

assistant.body: Great catch! There are two causes. First, email is pasted into the SQL with snprintf. A ' breaks the query syntax, and a hostile input turns it into SQL injection. PQexecParams sends the value separately from the $1 placeholder, so there is nothing to escape at all. Second, the PGresult from PQexec is never passed to PQclear. Once you are done reading a result, it has to be freed whether the query worked or not. I'm also adding a PQresultStatus check on the result.

turns.user: the ' thing is fixed. but now it returns -1 even for users that exist. the log just says find_user_id: with nothing after it

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous status check was wrong. PGRES_COMMAND_OK is what a command that returns no rows, like INSERT or UPDATE, gives back on success. A SELECT returns PGRES_TUPLES_OK, even when it finds zero rows. The query was succeeding, so it fell into the else branch with an empty error message. One comparison changes.

turns.user: oh wait sorry, email is only unique per tenant. take tenant_id as an argument too and filter on it

assistant.body: Here's the change: tenant_id becomes the first parameter and email moves to $2. paramTypes is NULL, so the server infers each type from the column. In other words, the caller can pass tenant_id as a plain string too. Note: nParams must match the number of placeholders.

sed -i '' 's/const char \*email)/const char *tenant, const char *email)/; s/params\[1\] = { email }/params[2] = { tenant, email }/; s/WHERE email = \$1/WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND email = $2/; s/1, NULL, params/2, NULL, params/' src/db/user.c
